problem:
$$
V=\text{Span}{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]},\,B={[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3\sqrt{14}}{14} \\ \frac{\sqrt{14}}{7} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{14}}{14}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V$ and an **orthonormal** basis $B$ of $V,$ given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $|a|+|b|+|c|?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Gram-Schmidt Process for Two Vectors

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 1 & -5 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $\text{Col}(A)$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ where $A$ and $B$ are given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $\text{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{c}{b}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}(A)$ is the span of the columns of $A.$ 

First, let's denote

$\,$ ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: Next, we find ${v}_{2}$, by using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{2}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{0\cdot \sqrt{2}+(-5)\cdot 1+1\cdot (-3)}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ -\frac{13}{3} \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $B={{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}={[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ -\frac{13}{3} \\ -1\end{aligned}]}$ is an orthogonal basis for $\text{Col}(A).$

Finally, $b=-\frac{13}{3},$ $c=-1,$ and  

$$
\frac{c}{b}=\frac{-1}{(-\frac{13}{3})}=\frac{3}{13}.
$$
